title: Coffee Frozen Yoghurt
changes_from_base: Low-fat yoghurt is drained only briefly and set with a little gelatine in hot milk flavoured with instant espresso, instead of a long-strained yoghurt with golden syrup.
summary: A smooth, creamy frozen yoghurt infused with the rich flavour of instant espresso. Serve straight from the ice-cream maker for soft-serve indulgence, or freeze for a firmer treat.

ingredients.note: 60 ml to soak the gelatine, 355 ml heated

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the 490 g yoghurt in a fine sieve over a jug in the fridge for 1-2 h until 120 ml liquid has run off; discard it.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: Sprinkle the 2 tsp gelatine over 60 ml milk, stand for 10 min stirring often.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat 355 ml milk with 200 g caster sugar and 6-7 tsp instant espresso powder, stirring until dissolved.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the bloomed gelatine until dissolved, then cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the cooled mixture into the drained yoghurt with 1 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn in the ice-cream maker until frozen, then serve soft or freeze in a sealed container for up to 2 days.

tips: Stir the espresso powder into the hot milk and sugar until fully dissolved, then cool the mixture to room temperature before stirring it into the drained yoghurt.
The gelatine needs the full 10 min to bloom in cold milk for a silky smooth texture.
Cool the mixture completely to room temperature before stirring into the yoghurt to prevent lumps.
Eat within 2 days for the creamiest texture; it becomes icy after longer storage.
storage: Store in a sealed freezer container for up to 2 days; beyond that it becomes icy.
